role.altitude: More of the week is the strategy meeting, the known-dataset check, and the sign-off. Retyping a standard command sequence and reading release notes for a known assay are no longer the long start of that work. She does not gain a right to issue a diagnostic result.
reach: medical scientist: how a biological question and the samples still available are set
biological technician: which columns a run file must carry
geneticist: which contrasts may be said about a person
skills_to_grow: reading a known-dataset test that failed
adding an assay label when no tagged release matches
spotting when a summary would inform a genetic predisposition
role.ambitious_version: A lab with no bioinformatics scientist pins a tested release for a standard expression study and books her for the sign-off and for goals that need a new method.

tasks.short: Consult researchers and recommend a computational strategy

steps.what: Read how researchers analyze problems in the note they sent
Read pipeline release notes for this assay and organism
Meet to hear sample limits and the wet-lab deadline
Consult researchers, then determine computational strategies and recommend technology based solutions

tasks.design: She still meets the researcher and chooses the strategy herself. A filter on the {DATA_PLATFORM} matches the organism, assay, and question she typed from the note to a tagged pipeline release and its test status. No sequence is sent to that filter, and the recommendation stays in the meeting.
tasks.previous_blocker: The fitting release was found by reading notes, because allowed releases were not tagged by assay and organism.
tasks.enabler_now: Tagged releases now carry the assay and a test status, so a filter can return the match before the meeting.
tasks.still_hard: Sample limits and what the wet lab can still collect are said in the meeting, and the strategy choice stays hers.
tasks.human_edge: She hears constraints the note left out and recommends a strategy the lab can run.
tasks.altitude: The meeting and the strategy choice stay hers. She no longer starts that meeting by reading release notes for an assay the catalog already tags.

reach.task: Set the biological question and the samples the lab can still collect
reach.learn: How that scientist sets assay limits and a deadline

evidence.claim: Before she recommends a strategy she reads which analysis releases fit the assay and organism.
Community bioinformatics pipelines are published as tagged releases with containers and tests.
Genetic data are a special category.
Research use of that data needs safeguards.

assumptions: This task ends when she has recommended a strategy in the meeting. Running the analysis and writing new source are other tasks.

The filter fields are organism, assay, and biological question. She types them while reading the note. If one is missing she asks in the meeting and types it before the filter runs. Sequence and health records stay out of the filter.
Reading release notes for a known assay is work she does today. The meeting and the spoken recommendation stay as they are.
A research computing specialist keeps the allowed release names. That hour is not taken off her net. She adds an assay label when no heading matches, and that hour is extra.
unknowns: Whether the researcher already names a release in the note.
Whether this company keeps tagged releases on the analysis platform.
research_questions: How often the consult note already names the release she would have looked up?

already_counted.description: Reading the note, the meeting, and the spoken recommendation stay in her remaining time.

incremental.description: She adds an assay label when the catalog has no heading for the note.
A research computing specialist keeps the allowed release names and test status.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low is zero when the researcher already named the release and she does not read pipeline notes. The high is 14 when every consult still has the full meeting and only the note-reading is shorter, after the hour she spends on new assay labels.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Provide statistical tools for genetic and expression work

steps.what: Read the request for genetic analysis, gene expression, or gene function determination
Write statistical and computational tools as the command sequence
Check the known-dataset result against the requested activity
Provide the accepted tools for biologically based activities such as measurement

tasks.design: For a standard genetic analysis, expression measure, or function test, a tagged release on the {DATA_PLATFORM} supplies the command sequence she used to write, using only the activity and column names she typed. She checks the known-dataset result and sends the run instructions she accepted. A method with no release is a different task.
tasks.previous_blocker: Each new file layout meant she wrote the command sequence again, even when a tested release already did that activity.
tasks.enabler_now: Tagged releases with tests can be pinned from the activity and the column names, after she has checked one known dataset.
tasks.still_hard: A result that would inform a person's genetic predisposition can be a diagnostic device, so this task stops at research run instructions.
tasks.human_edge: She decides whether a failed known-dataset result is a bad pin or a real mismatch with the activity.

ambition.what: A lab group with nobody to rewrite command sequences can run a pinned standard analysis after she has accepted the test.

tasks.altitude: She reviews the known-dataset result and sends the instructions. She no longer retypes the command sequence for an activity a release already covers. She does not gain a right to issue a clinical genetic result.

reach.task: Prepare the column layout the run will read
reach.learn: Which column names that release already expects

evidence.claim: She writes the command sequence for a standard genetic, expression, or function tool today.
Community bioinformatics pipelines are published as tagged releases with containers and tests.
Software that informs on a genetic predisposition can be an in vitro diagnostic device.
A Dutch works council can have to consent before a system that records who did the work.

assumptions: This task provides a standard tool. Writing a method that no release contains is the novel-tool task, and the per-dataset biological reading is the analysis task.

Fields she types from the request are the activity, one of genetic analysis, gene expression, or gene function, the column names, and the known-dataset id. If a column heading is missing she types it before the pin runs.
Writing that command sequence is work she does today. Sending the instructions still happens and is not treated as removed work.
A research computing specialist keeps the release pins. She adds a column name when the lab heading is not one the release lists. The pin hour of the specialist is not taken off her net.
unknowns: Whether a core facility already pins these releases.
Whether the run log is new enough to need works-council consent here.
research_questions: Which of these three activities already have a tested release in this company?

already_counted.description: Reading the request, checking the known-dataset result, and sending the instructions stay in her remaining time.

incremental.description: She adds a column name when the lab heading is not one the release lists.
A research computing specialist keeps the pinned release names.

approvals.approved_version: the run instructions she accepted in s3, including any command she rewrote there

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low is zero when a core facility already pinned the release and she does not write the command sequence. The high is 16 when she still checks every known-dataset result and only that writing is shorter, after the hour for new column names.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Analyze microarray, sequence, or proteomics datasets

steps.what: Confirm these files are raw microarray data, genomic sequence data, or proteomics data
Analyze large molecular datasets into QC metrics and a differential summary
Judge which contrasts matter for this study and reject a mismatched group
State the accepted findings for clinical or basic research purposes

tasks.design: After she confirms the assay, the sample ids, and the contrast, the pinned release on the {DATA_PLATFORM} computes the QC metrics and the differential summary. She judges what that summary means and sends only the findings she accepted. The note is a research summary, not a diagnostic issued to a patient.
tasks.previous_blocker: For each dataset she reassembled the QC metrics and the differential summary from the run, even when a tested release already computed them.
tasks.enabler_now: A pinned release can compute those metrics from the study fields she confirmed, and she still signs the biological reading.
tasks.still_hard: Harm from a wrong contrast is serious, and a summary that informs a genetic predisposition can be a diagnostic device. Cluster time that already runs is not her labour.
tasks.human_edge: She decides which differences matter for the study and whether any of them may be said about a person.

ambition.what: Sign the differential summary in the week the dataset arrives, including studies that waited while she reassembled the metrics.

tasks.altitude: Her time on a dataset goes to the biological reading and the sign-off. She does not gain a right to issue a patient diagnosis.

reach.task: Interpret a variant for a clinical research question
reach.learn: Which contrasts that geneticist allows to be said about a person

evidence.claim: She computes per-sample QC metrics and a differential summary when she analyzes a microarray, sequence, or proteomics dataset.
Community bioinformatics pipelines are published as tagged releases with containers and tests.
Genetic data are a special category.
Software that informs on a genetic predisposition can be an in vitro diagnostic device.

assumptions: This task is the per-dataset summary and her reading of it. Providing the standard tool, and writing a new method, are other tasks. Cluster time that already runs is not counted as her effort.
Fields she confirms are assay type, sample ids, and the contrast groups. She types a missing contrast before the summary runs. The summary states QC and statistics, not a diagnostic sentence.
Reassembling those metrics is work she does today. Sending the findings note still happens.
She adds a QC threshold when the assay has none yet. That hour is extra. A core facility that already computed the summary is outside her baseline.
unknowns: Whether these datasets are clinical or only basic research.
Whether a core facility already returns the QC and differential summary.
research_questions: What share of datasets already arrive with a signed summary from a core facility?

already_counted.description: Confirming the files, judging the contrast, and sending the findings stay in her remaining time.

incremental.description: She adds a QC threshold when the assay has none on the release.

approvals.approved_version: the findings note she accepted in s3, including any sentence she rewrote there

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low is zero when a core facility already computed the summary. The high is 18 when the contrast is clinical and she still recomputes much of the reading herself, after the hour for a new QC threshold.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Create a new computational tool for a research goal

steps.what: Read the research goals that standard tools cannot meet
Choose the novel computational approaches this goal needs
Write the source of that new tool against the known dataset

loop.input: The approach note, the known dataset named in the goal, and the expected calls she set
loop.output: Source text of the new tool
loop.check: Reject source whose calls on the known dataset miss the expected calls, or that implements a method she did not choose
loop.stop: One rewrite, then stop and leave the draft for her
loop.why_not_simpler: A tagged release cannot express an approach that no release contains

steps.what: Review whether the known dataset still yields the expected calls
Create the analytical tools required once the tests pass

tasks.design: She chooses the approach and the expected calls. A bounded loop on the {DATA_PLATFORM} drafts source from that note and the known dataset, and it stops when those calls match or after one retry. She reviews the calls and releases only the source she accepted.
tasks.previous_blocker: The first source had to be typed by hand before a known dataset could show that the approach failed.
tasks.enabler_now: A bounded draft can be checked against expected calls on a known dataset, and open-answer bioinformatics drafts are often wrong, so the check stays.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing the approach stays hers. If the released tool would inform a genetic predisposition, product rules for diagnostic software can apply, including later rules for AI inside such a device.
tasks.human_edge: She decides the approach. A test on a known dataset cannot invent the research goal.
tasks.altitude: She still chooses the approach and still accepts the source. The first typing of that source is no longer the long middle of the work.

reach.task: State the measurement the new tool must recover
reach.learn: Which control samples that biochemist trusts for the expected calls

evidence.claim: She writes new source when no existing tool meets the research goal.
Frontier models reached 17% accuracy on open-answer bioinformatics analyses, so a known-dataset check stays in front of a draft.
AI inside an in vitro diagnostic device falls under product-linked high-risk rules from 2 Aug 2028.
Research use of genetic data needs safeguards.

assumptions: This task starts only when no tagged release meets the goal. Standard command sequences are the tool-providing task.
She names the known dataset and writes the expected calls in the approach note before the draft runs. If either is missing, the draft does not run and she finishes the note.
Writing that source is work she does today. Releasing the accepted source still happens and is not treated as removed work.
She adds an expected call when a new goal has no test yet. That hour is extra. If a software engineer writes the source, this saving does not apply.
unknowns: Whether a software engineer already writes the novel source.
Whether the released tool will be used only in research.
research_questions: How often a new goal already has a known dataset with expected calls written down?

already_counted.description: Reading the goal, choosing the approach, reviewing the calls, and releasing the source stay in her remaining time.

incremental.description: She adds an expected call when a new goal has no known-dataset test yet.

approvals.approved_version: the tool source she accepted in s4, including any line she rewrote there

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low is zero when a software engineer already writes the source. The high is 15 when the known-dataset check fails often and she rewrites most of the draft, after the hour for new expected calls.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
